payload.body:
**ID:** MP-CGA-008 | **Priority:** P0 | **PRD refs:** FR7 | **Status:** draft
**Group:** MP Content Generation Agent (`mp-content-generation-agent`)

---

# Agent — persist rich provenance on successful newsletter create

## Summary

On a successful generation, the agent currently calls `contentGeneration.create(...)` with only `subject`, `description`, `content`, and `tickerId`. This ticket wires the seven provenance and token-usage fields (added to the contract in MP-CGA-001) into the newsletter create call so that every stored newsletter carries full auditability: which model generated it, which config version was active, what the prompt hash was, how many tokens were consumed, and which agent version ran.

## Scope

- In scope:
  - After a successful Vercel AI SDK `generateObject` call, compute and pass the following fields to `contentGeneration.create(...)`:
    - `model`: the model string from `config.openai.model` (or from the API response `model` field if available — use whichever is more reliable and document the choice).
    - `agentVersion`: same constant used in MP-CGA-007 (agent package version).
    - `configVersion`: a deterministic string derived from the config snapshot; use a short hash of the full validated config JSON (excluding `apiKey` — never include the secret in the hash input or the stored value). Document the hashing approach.
    - `promptHash`: SHA-256 (first 16 hex chars) of the effective system prompt + user prompt **after** placeholder substitution (i.e. the exact strings sent to the model). This makes prompt changes detectable in stored records.
    - `configSnapshotId`: if the Hermes runtime provides an immutable snapshot id in the invocation context, use it; otherwise fall back to `configVersion` (the config hash). Document the fallback.
    - `promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, `totalTokens`: read from `result.usage` in the Vercel AI SDK response (`promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, `totalTokens`). If `result.usage` is absent, store `null` and log a warning.
  - Unit tests: success path includes all provenance fields in the `create(...)` call; absent `response.usage` stores null for token fields.
- Out of scope:
  - The contract and DB schema changes for these fields (MP-CGA-001).
  - The diagnostic record (MP-CGA-007).
  - Provenance on skipped or failed runs (no newsletter row is written in those cases; the diagnostic covers observability).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a successful generation, `contentGeneration.create(...)` is called with all seven provenance fields populated (non-null) in the normal case.
- [ ] `model` is the string value of the model used for generation (from config or API response — document which, and why).
- [ ] `configVersion` is a deterministic hash that changes when any non-secret config field changes; the `apiKey` is explicitly excluded from the hash input (verified by test: two configs differing only in `apiKey` produce the same `configVersion`).
- [ ] `promptHash` reflects the exact system + user prompt strings sent to OpenAI after `{{sourceSummaries}}`, `{{tickerId}}`, and `{{date}}` substitution; it changes when the prompt template or source content changes.
- [ ] `configSnapshotId` is either the Hermes snapshot id (if available) or `configVersion` as fallback; the choice is documented in a code comment.
- [ ] When `response.usage` is absent, `promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, and `totalTokens` are stored as `null`; a warning is logged with `tickerId`.
- [ ] Unit tests (following `vitest-unit-testing` skill): full provenance path, absent `response.usage` path, config hash excludes `apiKey`, prompt hash sensitivity (different prompt → different hash).
- [ ] `pnpm code-quality` passes with no new errors.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: MP-CGA-001 (newsletter contract with provenance fields), MP-CGA-003 (config schema provides `model`, `systemPrompt`, `userPromptTemplate`)
- Blocks: none

## Stacked delivery

This ticket is independent of the observability stack (MP-CGA-005–007). It can be developed in a separate branch from MP-CGA-001 and MP-CGA-003's merged state, or stacked on top of MP-CGA-003 if that branch is not yet merged.

**Merge order:** Requires both MP-CGA-001 and MP-CGA-003 on `main` (or in the stack base). Can merge independently of MP-CGA-004 through MP-CGA-007 — provenance is only written on the success path, which those tickets do not block.

## Notes

- Use the Node.js built-in `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(input).digest('hex').slice(0, 16)` for `configVersion` and `promptHash` — no external dependency needed.
- For `configVersion`: serialize the validated config to JSON, remove the `apiKey` field, then hash. Use a stable serialization (e.g. `JSON.stringify` with sorted keys via a deterministic replacer) to avoid hash changes caused by property insertion order.
- For `promptHash`: concatenate `systemPrompt + "\n\n" + resolvedUserPrompt` before hashing. The resolved prompt is the one after placeholder substitution and source truncation (MP-CGA-004), so the hash captures the exact LLM input.
- Token usage from the Vercel AI SDK response: `result.usage?.promptTokens`, `result.usage?.completionTokens`, `result.usage?.totalTokens`. These are present on `generateObject` responses.

PRD: https://github.com/hyperjumptech/mediapulse/blob/prds/content-generation-agent-prd.md
